development: Blast announced on 2026-10-02 that the L2 will wind down, with a staged Ethereum withdrawal process that directly affects Blast USDB lifecycle, redemption operations, and native-yield context.
confirmed: Blast announced an orderly L2 wind-down.
Users were instructed to withdraw assets to Ethereum.
Blast said withdrawals would be temporarily unavailable while Lido-linked assets were unwound, a process expected to take about one week.
Blast said the withdrawal delay would be reduced to 24 hours after the Lido unwind.
Normal Blast-interface withdrawals are planned through October 26, 2026.
After October 26, Blast said users can still withdraw by interacting directly with the bridge contracts on Ethereum L1.
not_inferred: completed Blast chain shutdown as of October 8
final end date for all USDB yield accrual
universal withdrawal success for every contract or user configuration

canonical_decision.reason: The network wind-down materially changes Blast USDB lifecycle, withdrawal operations, and native-yield context while preserving a stated bridge exit path.

notes: Canonical lifecycle state is winding_down. SOG keeps the Blast deployment operational until effective termination is independently verified.
